Hello,

{TABLE}

Kind regards

findings.explanation: The invoice bills 10, but only 8 has been received and not yet invoiced, so 2 is still to come, worth GBP 212.00. Holding the invoice until the rest is delivered fits, as the vendor should not be paid for goods not yet received.

The unit cost is GBP 106.00 against GBP 100.00 on the latest posted invoice line, compared with 1 posted invoice line, a difference of 6% (GBP 60.00). This matches the order check, so the same price question applies and the vendor should confirm it.

This freight line of GBP 150.00 has no purchase order or receipt behind it, so it would not reach the item cost. Assigning it as an item charge fits, as the freight relates to the goods being invoiced.
This item charge line of GBP 75.00 has a quantity of 1 not yet assigned to receipt lines, so the invoice cannot be posted until it is. Assigning it to the receipt lines is the required step.

A posted invoice from the same vendor has a vendor invoice number that matches this one once spaces and symbols are removed, and the same amount of GBP 1,535.00. Querying it before posting avoids paying the same invoice twice.
